content.tldr: Zero-shot relies solely on pretrained weights, few-shot supplies in-context input-output demonstrations, and Chain-of-Thought prompts the model to generate intermediate reasoning steps before concluding.
content.simple_explanation: Zero-shot prompting provides an instruction without any prior demonstration, testing the model's generalized pretraining. Few-shot in-context learning supplies 2-5 explicit exemplars showing the desired format, edge-case handling, and style without modifying model weights. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting instructs the model to 'think step by step', giving the autoregressive transformer intermediate scratchpad tokens where it can compute state representations for complex multi-hop logic.
content.real_world_example: Asking an intern to solve a tax deduction: zero-shot is 'calculate this return'; few-shot provides two past audited returns as formatting guides; Chain-of-Thought requires showing the arithmetic scratch work on paper before writing the final refund number.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Standard transformers struggle with multi-step math and logic in direct generation because next-token prediction cannot perform dynamic backtracking. Generating CoT scratchpad tokens provides the computational depth required to avoid premature greedy token hallucinations.
